plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Nüsslein-Volhard & Wieschaus (30 October 1980, Nature 287: 795–801) and Lewis (7 December 1978, Nature 276: 565–570) Drosophila segmentation hierarchy chart shows Maternal gradient (Bicoid anterior-to-posterior concentration curve) -> Gap genes -> Pair-rule 7-stripe genes -> 14 Segment-polarity stripes -> 8 Colinear Homeotic (Hox) selector genes.

teach_overlay.detail: Inked Nüsslein-Volhard & Wieschaus (30 October 1980, Nature 287: 795–801) and Lewis (7 December 1978, Nature 276: 565–570) Drosophila segmentation hierarchy chart on period paper showing Maternal gradient (Bicoid anterior-to-posterior concentration curve) -> Gap genes -> Pair-rule 7-stripe genes -> 14 Segment-polarity stripes -> 8 Colinear Homeotic (Hox) selector genes
teach_overlay.scale: building a body from a single round egg is like painting a map on a blank globe — first a smooth gradient of maternal ink marks the North Pole as the head, then three waves of stencil genes divide the globe into fourteen numbered stripes, and finally each stripe reads its own Hox address code
